gitCommit.subject: Put a released transfer back to a type that counts
gitCommit.body:
Put a released transfer back to a type that counts

Nullifying the FK left the surviving row typed transfer_in or
transfer_out with nothing to point at. Every total filters for income or
expense, and RECONCILABLE_TYPES excludes transfers, so that row dropped
out of the user's totals and no future statement upload could ever pair
it again — the money would have quietly vanished.

It now goes back to income or variable_expense by the sign of its amount,
which both restores it to the totals and makes it eligible for
reconciliation when the other account's statement is uploaded. A
fixed_expense comes back as variable_expense; the original type is not
recorded anywhere, and sign is the only honest reconstruction.

Also replaces dependent: :nullify with an explicit callback. The has_one
released a single pointer, so two rows referencing the same transaction
still hit the foreign key — which is what the new spec caught.

Trimmed the commentary on this branch back to the two places where the
reason is not visible in the code.
